Model bounded capabilities and search-usage events without assuming prices, plans or customer facts. Support deterministic validation and aggregation for searches used, successful searches, degraded searches and remaining quota only when an explicit limit is supplied. Never store raw lead contact data, access codes, cookies, tokens or free-form notes. Include tests for invalid limits, replay-safe event IDs, aggregation and privacy. Keep this as an adapter-ready domain layer; do not wire billing, external APIs, production deployment or user communications.

findings: src/providers/niche-mapper.ts recognizes barbería and barberia as Peluquerías aliases but omits barberías and barberias; getNicheDiscoveryStrategy requires an exact normalized alias match, so Barberías returns null.

src/providers/niche-relevance.ts falls back to literal niche matching for unknown queries. Consequently, Barberías with evidence name Barbería López and taxonomy hairdresser scores 0, whereas the recognized singular query uses the hairdresser strategy.

src/providers/osm-business-search.ts gives unknown niches empty canonical filters and invokes the initial Overpass query without a text term. For Barberías this produces empty-regex selectors before subsequent literal text expansion, potentially spending discovery budget on unrelated entities.

The single recommended change is adding barberías and barberias to the existing Peluquerías aliases. Add regression assertions in src/providers/osm-logic.test.ts for singular/plural strategy equivalence and in src/providers/niche-relevance.test.ts for Barberías matching Barbería López and hairdresser taxonomy while rejecting restaurante evidence. The supplied tests currently contain no barber-query regression cases.
